Assess the predecessor's claim that a real Ry(2 arccos|A_ij|) alone produces this full signed/complex target; it is now a proposed magnitude stage, not an assumed correct oracle. Do not restrict entries to nonnegative reals or silently exclude zero entries.

For each existing entry z=A_ij, prove the sharp normalized-state domain and give an explicit two-by-two unitary completion when it is valid. Separate z=0,0<|z|<1,|z|=1 and |z|>1, with exact angles, signed/complex counterexamples and a phase-aware correction. Distinguish correctness on input |0> from equality of full unitary extensions and inverse actions; retain phases across coherent index superpositions. Distinguish vacuous entry-wise conditions and zero-space unitary equations from existence of a normalized label input. For a nonempty matrix derive preprocessing by a known M>0 dominating its entry max norm, including the all-zero case and loose upper bounds.

Only under a supplied nonempty square matching/permutation plus clean entry-access interface, with integer slot budget s>=1 and an exact decomposition of A, derive the projected block and its positive scale. Specify register order, PREP, SELECT and unprepare. Explain why an entry bound alone does not supply that interface, why duplicated nonzero pieces are invalid, why rectangular embedding/padding is additional work, and when postselected normalization is undefined.

reference_answer:
Write v(z)=(z,s_z)^T, r=|z| and s_z=sqrt(1-r^2), with the stipulated real nonnegative square root. For each existing entry, this is defined and has norm one exactly when r<=1: r^2+s_z^2=1. In that closed disk, U_z=[[z,-s_z],[s_z,conj(z)]] has unit columns and column inner product -conj(z)s_z+s_z conj(z)=0, so U_z†U_z=I. Its first column is v(z). Direct sum of these blocks on the retained orthogonal labels |i>|j> gives an ideal unitary entry oracle. This proves existence, not uniqueness of its second column or an efficient circuit. For r>1 the required real square root is undefined; even an imaginary continuation i sqrt(r^2-1) makes the column's squared norm2r^2-1>1. No unitary can produce that advertised column from a unit input.

Use Ry(theta)=[[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]]. The proposed magnitude stage R_z=Ry(2 arccos r) produces (r,s_z), not generally(z,s_z). At z=0 its angle is pi and the output is |1>; for0<r<1 its angle is strictly between0 and pi and both coefficients are nonzero; at r=1 its angle is0, the second coefficient vanishes and the desired state is z|0>, still valid. At r>1 no real magnitude angle exists. Thus, for a finite nonempty matrix, strict max norm below1 gives the positive gap 1-||A||_max and keeps s_z positive, but without a specified error bound and implemented guards it does NOT guarantee a safe rounded-entry implementation; it still does not ensure two populated branches, an angle below pi at every entry or sign/phase correctness.

Take z=-1/2 or z=i/2. The proposed stage gives(1/2,sqrt(3)/2); the target's first coefficient instead is -1/2 or i/2 while its second is the SAME positive sqrt(3)/2. Any global phase relating them would have to be1 by the second coefficient, contradicting the first. These strict-interior witnesses refute the old active correctness assertion, not existence of a better oracle. At unit modulus, two labels with z=1 and z=-1 change (|a>+|b>)|0>/sqrt2 into (|a>-|b>)|0>/sqrt2. A phase that is global for one fixed label is relative across coherent labels and cannot be dropped.

For r>0 let q=z/r and D_z=diag(q,1); at r=0 choose q=1,D_z=I, avoiding division by zero. Then C_z=D_z R_z has first column v(z). But C_z=[[z,-q s_z],[s_z,r]]=U_z diag(1,q), so generally C_z is NOT U_z: their second columns and inverse actions differ. For example at z=-1/2 the second columns are opposite. If U_z itself is required, the additional input phase E_z=diag(1,conj(q)) gives U_z=D_z R_z E_z, with the same zero convention. Each construction must be composed as the actual chosen unitary, not replaced by a first-column identity. If q=e^(i phi), D_z=e^(i phi/2)Rz(-phi) under Rz(t)=diag(e^(-it/2),e^(it/2)); the prefactor is label dependent and not free to discard. For real signed z, Ry(2 arccos z) is a separate correct completion, with angles in[0,2pi] and angle2pi at z=-1. A stored fractional-angle format restricted to[0,1) cannot represent arccos(-1)/pi=1 without an explicit endpoint mechanism. None of these are a proof of the old magnitude-only assertion.

If either row or column set is empty, the entry set is empty: there is no ordinary maximum absolute entry, so the retained notation ||A||_max has no value there. Do not totalize it by zero. The entry-wise closed-disk condition is vacuous, and the label space C^rows tensor C^cols is zero dimensional, with no normalized vector. The unique map on that space (also on signal tensor that space) satisfies U†U=I=0 vacuously; this is not a physical normalized-input oracle promise. Qubit registers have positive dimension. The max-based formulas below are conditional on a nonempty entry set, not a silent exclusion of emptiness from the assessment. Non-power-of-two or rectangular label encodings into qubit registers likewise need an explicit carrier adapter, not an assumed free identification.

For nonempty A choose a KNOWN M>0 with M>=||A||_max and build the entry target for A/M. All entries then lie in the closed disk. For nonempty zero A use, for instance,M=1, not0/0 or a zero normalization factor. A strict M>||A||_max makes the magnitudes strictly below1, but still leaves zero entries with an unpopulated first branch. Computing a bound/max and proving a quantitative precision guard are not free preprocessing.

Here is the precise conditional sparse calculation. Suppose A is N-by-N with N>=1, s>=1, supplied permutations c_l of[N], and pieces B_l whose entries are (B_l)_ij=A_(c_l(j),j) delta_(i,c_l(j)), with the EXACT identity sum_l B_l=A. This decomposition, coherent permutation access and phase-correct CLEAN entry loading are additional source-interface data, not consequences of an entry bound. Fix register order(signal a,slot L,system H). Let P|0_L>=s^(-1/2)sum_l|l>, let O load v(A_(c_l(j),j)/M) on a while retaining(l,j) and restoring all scratch to zero, and let S|l>|j>=|l>|c_l(j)>. Then W=(I_a tensor P† tensor I_H)(I_a tensor S)O(I_a tensor P tensor I_H) is unitary. Projection gives <0_a,0_L,i|W|0_a,0_L,j>=(1/(sM))sum_l A_(c_l(j),j)delta_(i,c_l(j))=A_ij/(sM). Thus the positive scale is alpha=sM. If s is not a power of two, an implementation of P/padding is a further obligation; the source's Hadamard special case does not provide it for free. Rectangular A needs a separately specified square embedding/projection and access/cost adapter before this theorem applies.

A duplicate-piece error is concrete: for A=[1/2], s=2,M=1 and c_0=c_1=identity with both pieces [1/2], their sum is[1], not A. The actual projected block is[1/2], whereas the claimed A/(sM) is[1/4]. Exact decomposition therefore matters. Nor does entry norm alone give scale1 for general A: the N-by-N all-ones matrix has entry max1 but operator normN. A block compression forces alpha>=||A||_op; it does not prove optimality of sM. Equality of sM with s||A||_max requires choosing the actual POSITIVE max, not a loose M or zero A. With a normalized system input psi, success probability is ||A psi||^2/(sM)^2; only if A psi!=0 is the conditional successful state A psi/||A psi|| defined. Zero A can use padded s=1,M=1 and a signal-X entry oracle, giving a valid zero block and probability0, not a normalized zero state or alpha0.

Precision is a separate mathematical interface. For0<delta<1, v(1)=(1,0) and v(1-delta)=(1-delta,sqrt(2delta-delta^2)) differ in squared Euclidean norm2delta, hence error sqrt(2delta); no uniform O(delta) endpoint state-error bound follows. More generally, for z,w in the disk with |z-w|<=delta, ||v(z)-v(w)||^2=|z-w|^2+(s_z-s_w)^2<=delta^2+2delta, using |sqrt(a)-sqrt(b)|^2<=|a-b| and ||z|^2-|w|^2|<=2delta. For the fixed family U_z above, (U_z-U_w)†(U_z-U_w)=||v(z)-v(w)||^2 I, so the SAME bound controls its whole operator-norm difference. It does not control arbitrary completions from their first columns. Indeed C_epsilon and C_(-epsilon),0<epsilon<1, have first-column difference2epsilon but whole operator-norm difference2: their second-column phases differ. If a rounded value tilde_z leaves the disk, an explicitly implemented radial clipping w can restore validity but changes the loaded target. For true z in the disk and |tilde_z-z|<=eta, elementary triangle bounds give |w-z|<=2eta; combine with the preceding bound and charge clipping/arithmetic error rather than claiming exact original loading.

For the narrower stored-angle primitive, if theta=sum_(k=1)^d b_k 2^(-k) is actually supplied exactly in[0,1), same-axis rotations compose additively: the d corresponding single-bit-controlled Ry(2pi*2^(-k)) gates realize Ry(2pi theta). This is d logical arbitrary controlled rotations, not d Clifford+T gates. If a phase fraction u=phi/(2pi) is supplied in d_p bits, analogous bit-controlled diagonal phases use d_p gates for D_z; realizing U_z via both D_z and E_z uses2d_p such phases, in addition to d_m magnitude rotations. These conditional counts exclude data production, zero flags, scratch, inverse computation, PREP/SELECT and elementary synthesis, and do not assert that arbitrary real/complex entries possess exact finite-bit angle/phase representations. Approximate stored parameters require the separate error accounting just proved.

Finally a legitimate coherent finite-word implementation must compute the stored magnitude/angle/phase data without changing the label, apply the chosen signal circuit, then reverse that SAME computation to clean all data and scratch BEFORE any later matching permutation changes j. If C_data is implemented as one entry-bit query followed by reversible arithmetic, the explicit C_data–signal–C_data† realization uses one forward and one inverse entry query, plus arithmetic and its inverse; this is a conditional ledger, not free inverse access or a universal minimal count. Scratch, magnitude/phase computation (including zero handling), transcendental approximations, controlled rotations/phases, PREP, SELECT, unused-code extensions, gate-synthesis precision, readout and amplification must all be specified/costed separately where used. Unknown-unitary control or a generic efficient phase/matching oracle is not supplied by ideal existence. This answer supplies a corrected theorem and transparent assumption change, not current-engine admission, a compiler theorem or a new kernel proof.
